facts.fact: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)
facts.quote: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)

facts.fact: P(exactly one) = P(A) + P(B) − 2P(A ∩ B), so P(A) + P(B) = 2p + q and P(A ∪ B) = p + q
P(Ā) + P(B̄) = 2 − 2p − q (B true, A false); P(Ā ∩ B̄) = 1 − P(A ∪ B) = 1 − p − q (C true)
P((A ∩ B)|(A ∪ B)) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A ∪ B) = p/(p + q) (D true)

reason: Old rows use the addition rule with numbers, but none handles "exactly one of A and B", De Morgan's complement of a union, or a conditional on the union.
